evidence.claim: Google documents agy --help as the basic CLI verification command.
Launching agy starts the Antigravity CLI and establishes a workspace context before agent work begins.
Antigravity CLI asks the user to trust a workspace before granting the agent permission to read, edit, and execute files there.
Antigravity CLI can list models available to the current environment; the actual model list is volatile and should never be hard-coded into durable course claims.
Antigravity CLI accepts a model selection flag for a session; model names remain version- and account-sensitive.

Antigravity CLI exposes Tool Permission configuration. Current documented modes include request-review, proceed-in-sandbox, always-proceed, and strict; these labels are version-sensitive and must be rechecked before publication.
Google's Antigravity codelab uses the Agent Skills ecosystem and documents project-scope installation under the .agents directory; Antigravity CLI is included as a supported target in that workflow.
Antigravity CLI supports workspace-level MCP configuration under .agents/mcp_config.json.
Antigravity CLI exposes an interactive MCP status view so the user can inspect configured external tool connections.

Google's MCP example explicitly warns that an MCP server may expose destructive operations unless underlying service permissions constrain them; MCP connectivity is therefore a trust and authorization boundary, not just a convenience feature.
Antigravity CLI exposes a flag that automatically approves tool permissions; Google labels the behavior as dangerous and it must not be the normal course workflow.
